A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hierarchical-filtering study. Their full text, figures, equations and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: v2 reports original transformer experiments on root classification, masked language modeling, calibration, attention patterns and ancestor probing, including supplementary experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in the main text and Appendix E, including comparisons with BP and analyses of learned representations.

M1.justification: The filtering procedure, trained transformer architecture, objectives, readouts and BP-emulating recursions are retained. The added feedforward construction elaborates an existing step rather than changing the proposed algorithm or trained model.

E1.justification: Both use the same synthetic hierarchical grammars, filtering levels, root-classification and single-symbol MLM tasks, ancestor probing, and filtered or uniformly generated out-of-sample inputs.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same matched and mismatched BP_k oracles and comparisons between training from scratch and MLM pretraining with frozen or unfrozen encoders.

E3.justification: The stated architecture, optimizer, masking, train/test filtering and probing procedures are unchanged. The shortened sample-size range displayed in the root-classification plot omits results without documenting a revised experimental procedure.

E4.justification: The depth ablation, alternative-grammar checks, distribution-mismatch analyses, attention maps and restricted-position probing experiments are retained. v2 Appendix D corresponds to v3 Appendix E.

E5.justification: Both disclose the same grammar seeds and retain the same statistical reporting practices. Neither adds repeated-training-run summaries, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 Figure 2(a) omits the P = 2^20 points shown for filtered training in v2 Figure 3. The MLM BP reference accuracies also change slightly between v2 Figure 5 and v3 Figure 3(a), for example approximately 0.618 to 0.609 for ktest = 2. The principal experimental trends remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix F adds Equation 23 constructing message products through squared activations, discusses O(q^3) general and O(q^2) sparse hidden-unit requirements, and explains ReLU approximation and residual cancellation. v2 Appendix E relied on universal approximation for this feedforward step; the surrounding recurrences are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: tunable hierarchical filtering, approximately optimal and calibrated inference, sequential learning of correlations, and hierarchical internal representations compatible with BP.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly proposes a tentative connection to motif learning, interpreting progressively integrated ancestral blocks as increasingly long motifs. Existing qualifications concerning fixed tree topology and the idealized BP implementation remain.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement changes the code repository destination from tree-language-paper-submission to tree-language. The documented software, training hyperparameters, data-generation seeds and probing details are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Wu, Thalmann and Schulz (2023) to support the new motif-learning connection. Other bibliography changes mainly update publication information for works already cited in v2.

P1.justification: The detailed BP description moves from Section 2.4 to Appendix B, and references move before the appendices. Local wording and cross-reference edits accompany added affiliation, funding and generic impact text; most of the narrative is retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column layout with wrapped figures to two columns. v2 Figures 3/4 become v3 Figure 2, and Figures 5/7 become Figure 3. The BP diagram is rearranged and relocated, other figures are resized or repositioned, and the MLM caption is corrected.

improvement.justification: The explicit feedforward construction in Appendix F makes the BP-embedding argument easier to assess than v2's universal-approximation appeal, including useful width and activation qualifications. Caption and cross-reference corrections also improve clarity. The omitted large-sample points and small BP-reference revisions leave the principal empirical conclusions intact, so the overall gain is limited.
